title: Response Slab — germinal PRD notes
content:
Top-level idea: 'Response Slab' = a composable response layer that assembles model outputs from small, graded building blocks (slabs) to control cost, latency and quality per request.

Context / motivation:
- Customers need predictable unit economics but varied experience per user/route (e.g., search assistant vs. writing assistant).
- Current approach toggles between full-model and cheap-model fallbacks; coarse and binary.
- Goal: give product teams fine-grained levers to shape output (verbosity, factuality checks, style) while surfacing clear costing and latency tradeoffs.

Rough concept/architecture notes:
- A 'slab' = a self-contained response component: e.g., short summary slab, quote-extract slab, citation-check slab, followup-suggestion slab. Each slab has metadata: expected token cost, latency distribution, quality score (heuristic/eval-derived), compatibility tags.
- Response Slab Engine: orchestrates slabs in pipeline or parallel, decides ordering, aggregation, trimming. Supports: sequential chaining, parallel multiplexing, speculative execution with early-stops.
- API model: client requests an ordered slab-plan (explicit) OR a policy (ruleset) that maps request signals -> slab-plan. Redwood can offer default policies (cost-first, fidelity-first, hybrid).
- Fallbacks: when a slab misses latency/quality, engine can 1) omit, 2) replace with cheaper stub slab, 3) request a compensating slab (e.g., add clarifying question slab).

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to compose a response from small slabs so I can A/B different compositions without re-training models.
- As an SRE, I want slab-level telemetry so I can see which slabs drive cost/latency regressions.
- As an enterprise customer, I want to pin 'sensitive' slabs to private-deploy models for auditability while letting other slabs run on hosted cheaper models.
- As an API consumer, I want a budget cap that ensures per-response slabs don't exceed X tokens and get gracefully truncated/trimmed.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: slab-plan schema + policy reference in request payload documented (examples).
- Engine: can execute 3 slab types in a pipeline (summary, extract, polish) with correct aggregation and a single coherent output.
- Telemetry: per-slab token cost, latency p50/p95, error rate surfaced in console and tracing.
- Fallback: implement 'omit' and 'replace-stub' fallback modes.

Design notes / UX snippets:
- Console: slab catalog view (cards) showing typical token cost, target latency, suggested use-cases, demo output.
- Quickstart: "Build a 2-slab assistant" template (summary + suggestion) with sample slab-plan JSON and cost estimate preview.
- SDK: helpers to create slab plans from templates; validation that total expected tokens <= budget.

Open questions / research tasks:
- How to measure slab-level 'quality score' automatically? Options: lightweight heuristics (n-gram overlap to references), small eval harnesses, or curated human eval. Tradeoffs: cost/time.
- Compatibility: some slabs depend on model context size (long-extract slab needs long seq). How to annotate and enforce?
- Aggregation semantics: simple concatenation vs. structured merge vs. reranker to produce final single-turn output. Which is best for UX?
- Caching & KV reuse: slabs that rely on prior conversation state should use KV cache to avoid re-generation. Need slab-level cache keys.
- Billing surface: per-slab metering vs. aggregated per-request. UX implications for customers and SDK.

Experiment ideas / small bets:
- Start with 3 slab templates (summary, extract-quote, short-followup). Run internal A/B on playground flows comparing slab assembly vs monolithic prompt for cost & quality.
- Offer a 'cost-forecast' API for a slab-plan that returns expected token range and 90th-percentile latency given historical profile.
- Try a 'speculative polish' slab: run cheap base model for main content, and in parallel run a smaller 'polish' slab that post-processes language; if polish completes within latency SLO, swap in.

Implementation risks & mitigation:
- Risk: complexity of assembly leads to inconsistent tone/voice. Mitigation: provide 'style slab' that normalizes output, or an optional unified post-polish slab.
- Risk: explosion of slab types causing catalog maintenance burden. Mitigation: curate small opinionated default set + plugin model for power users.

Next concrete todos:
- [ ] Draft slab-plan JSON schema (fields: id, type, params, expected_tokens, model_constraints, fallback_mode).
- [ ] Prototype 3-slab pipeline in local inference playground; log per-slab metrics.
- [ ] Fast experiment: 50 internal sessions compare cost/quality vs baseline.
- [ ] Sketch console slab-catalog UI (card states, cost badges).

Notes to self: keep MVP tiny. Focus on one product flow (assistant help widget) where structured slabs feel natural (summary + citation + quick-actions).

Random fragments / brainstormed names for product marketing:
- "Slab Compose"
- "Layered Responses"
- "Response Fabric"

End-of-file scratch addendum:
- Consider policy integration with Optimize: recommend slab plans based on route-level traffic profile.
- Could map slab types to Redwood Optimize recommendations (e.g., quantized model for extract slabs).

-- Sahil
